notes: Summary: Veridian builds inference controllers for high-value industrial lines; evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency decisioning in edge gateways.
Primary ask: hard latency SLOs (p95 < 150ms for control path), deterministic throughput for 1k-3k concurrent inference requests per factory shift, and an enterprise SLA with credits for downtime.
Redwood POC: 4-GPU reserved pool (A100-equivalent) + autoscale burst to 6 GPUs; target sustained throughput 2,000 rps of short chat/telemetry inference (token light).
Throughput guarantees discussed: baseline reserved capacity to support 1k rps steady state with documented benchmarking; additional burst capacity with 2–3x headroom for seasonal peaks.
Latency SLOs: customer requests p95 < 150ms, p99 < 450ms for <=1k tokens. Redwood proposed p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms for first offer; Liam to run targeted kernel tuning to hit p95 150ms in POC.
Uptime / SLA negotiation: Veridian legal wants 99.99% (≤4.3 min downtime/month) with graduated credits. Redwood initial standard for Dedicated = 99.9% (≤43 min/month).
Proposed credit schedule (initial negotiate):
- 99.99%+ : no credits (target for enterprise add-on)
- 99.95%–99.99% : 10% service credit
- 99.9%–99.95% : 25% service credit
- <99.9% : 50% service credit / termination right after repeated breaches
Customer pushback: wants replacement credits tied to business impact (factory-loss metric) and a clear escalation path; legal asked to map credits to ARR multiples — negotiating now.

Maintenance windows: Veridian requires predictable monthly maintenance window localized to 02:00–04:00 local factory time (multiple timezones). Redwood prefers rolling maintenance with 48-hour notice; negotiating pinned maintenance windows for Dedicated customers.

Support / Response times: Veridian requires P1 15m acknowledgement, P1 mitigation 1 hour; P2 initial response 1 hour, P3 4 hours. Redwood standard SLAs: P1 30m acknowledgement, 4h mitigation. SE/Liam proposed Premium SME on-call add-on to meet 1h mitigation for P1.

Fallback and graceful degradation: need automatic routing to a slightly smaller model variant in a different region if Dedicated pool exhausted; acceptance criteria: failover < 2s and degrade latency by less than 2x.

Security/compliance: must support SSO/SAML, KMS integration for keys (HSM optional), audit logs forwarded to customer's SIEM, and 7yr retention for certain telemetry fields. Private deployment option being scoped.

- Week 1: baseline benchmarks (latency, p95/p99) on 4-GPU reserved cluster — benchmark script & dataset in Drive (link above).
- Week 2: kernel tuning + quantization profile testing; measure cost delta and quality regression (target <1% regression).
- Week 3: resilience tests (failover, maintenance window simulation) and SLA outage simulation to validate credit calculations.
